claim: MCF-7 breast cancer cells were adapted to increasing concentrations of either doxorubicin or epirubicin to a maximum tolerated dose of 98.1 nM (DoxR cells) or 852 nM (EpiR cells), respectively, in a stepwise manner and over several months.
source: Briefly, these models were generated from human MCF-7 breast cancer cells, adapted to increasing concentrations of either doxorubicin or epirubicin to a maximum tolerated dose of 98.1 nM (DoxR cells) or 852 nM (EpiR cells), respectively, in a stepwise manner and over several months (Hembruff et al., 2008; Figure 1a).
evidence: The manuscript cites Hembruff et al., 2008 as the source of this methodology and references Figure 1a showing the model.

claim: Parental control cells (Control cells) were maintained in DMSO throughout the extensive selection process.
source: Parental control cells (Control cells) were maintained in DMSO throughout the extensive selection process (Hembruff et al., 2008; Figure 1a).
evidence: The manuscript cites Hembruff et al., 2008 and references Figure 1a.

claim: Augmenting intracellular drug levels by inhibiting ABC transporter activity in DoxR or EpiR has little effect on cell survival.
source: Indeed, augmenting intracellular drug levels by inhibiting ABC transporter activity in DoxR or EpiR has little effect on cell survival, highlighting the importance of adaptation mechanisms separate from that of the ABC transporters and independent of drug concentration (Hembruff et al., 2008).
evidence: The manuscript cites Hembruff et al., 2008 as the source of this finding.

claim: DoxR and EpiR cells maintained in culture with a stable dose of their respective drug grew slower than Control cells without treatment.

evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1b.
